note: Schema 1 recorded every non-PSX guest as mode 'native-bridge' against /dev/native0 guest kinds. That bridge does not exist in PowerEngine and has been removed; see the 'Removed: the native-bridge mock' section of docs/VIRTUA_PLATFORM.md. Each guest now reaches the device by one of two real routes, chosen by whether the guest CPU is the host CPU.

modes.static-recompilation: guest CPU is not ARMv7; guest code is translated to C ahead of time and compiled for Cortex-A7
modes.direct-execution: guest CPU is ARMv7, same as the host; guest instructions run untranslated and the guest's OS is reimplemented around them (the WINE model)

gba.note: Studio drives this automatically; the previous 'Native' checkbox and its /dev/native0 launcher are gone.

containers: unpacked title directory (the eboot.bin + sce_sys/ tree of a dumped title)
vita.pkg_reader: header, metadata records and item table are decrypted with the format's own published key: key type at 0xE4, types 2-4 derive the AES-128-CTR key by ECB-encrypting the package riv, type 1 uses the key directly. The key is only accepted when the decrypted item table is self-consistent (offsets inside the data area, printable ASCII names). Yields the item list, sce_sys/param.sfo and the plaintext sce_pfs/pflist.
vita.pfs_reader: the second layer. Keyed by the title's own 16-byte klicensee, read from a NoNpDrm work.bin, a .rif or a zRIF (SceNpDrmLicense, 0x200 bytes; content id at 0x10, key at 0x50). Decryption runs through the vendored psvpfsparser in extra/vita2hos/external/Vita3K/external/psvpfstools.
vita.licence_verification: before any decryption, the candidate klicensee is checked against the title's own sce_pfs/files.db: the secret is derived with scePfsUtilGetSecret from the header's files_salt, image_spec and key_id, and HMAC-SHA1 over the header with header_icv and rsa_sig0 zeroed must reproduce header_icv. A licence for another title derives a different signature and is rejected by name, so a wrong licence can never silently decrypt to garbage and the search order is a matter of speed only.
licence_search: work.bin, license.rif, <TITLEID>.rif, <TITLEID>.zrif, *.rif, *.zrif beside the container and one level up
sce_sys/package/temp.bin inside a package (recognised, and refused as the placeholder it is)
vita.staging: the whole decrypted title is written as data/, the PFS metadata and the licence as container/, and eboot.bin additionally as executable. The staged module is re-read and re-classified after decryption, so a truncated or mis-assembled PFS extraction is caught rather than packaged.

samples.branding/vita/pkg/terraria.pkg: opens: 103 items, content id EP4040-PCSB00405_00-TERRARIA00000001, param.sfo Terraria / PCSB00405 / gd / 01.00, 78 PFS-protected files. No licence for PCSB00405 exists on this machine, so it is refused by title and by the list of places searched. Given the PCSE00317 licence instead, the refusal becomes a signature mismatch naming both digests — which is the per-title check working, not failing.
samples.branding/vita/standard/PCSE00317/: an already-decrypted dump, accepted whether the directory or its eboot.bin is selected: no sce_pfs, so no licence is wanted, and the whole title stages as data/ (67 files, 33,564,888 bytes).

horizon.nsp_reader_unkeyed: the outer PFS0 partition, the .cnmt.xml content list and the ticket parse with no key at all: title id, content meta type, every NCA in the package, the ticket rights id and title key
horizon.nsp_reader_keyed: the NCA header is AES-128-XTS under header_key with Nintendo's big-endian sector tweak; with a prod.keys present Studio decrypts it and walks the FS headers to both program sections — the ExeFS PFS0 and the RomFS
horizon.nsp_key_miss: with no prod.keys the unkeyed tier still reads in full and the refusal names header_key and lists the paths searched, rather than calling the whole package encrypted.
horizon.staging: the whole program is written as data/: every ExeFS entry under data/exefs/ (main, main.npdm, rtld, sdk, subsdk0..n), the decrypted RomFS image verbatim as data/romfs.bin, and the Control NCA icon as data/control/. The ticket, cert and .cnmt.xml go to container/, and the ExeFS main additionally to executable. RomFS is staged as an image rather than unpacked: its names are UTF-8 and case-sensitive and the host filesystem here is neither, so an unpack would be a re-encoding rather than a copy.
horizon.arch_source: the ExeFS main.npdm — the process manifest Horizon's own loader reads. Its flags byte states the instruction set outright. The entry-instruction probe is kept as a second, independent reading and a disagreement is reported, but it cannot always answer: an NSO .text is LZ4 and need not open with a branch.

ExeFS main 2,708,936 / main.npdm 1,476 / rtld 7,112 / sdk 4,409,751 / subsdk0 11,491,034 / subsdk1 3,277,207. RomFS 157,904,376 bytes, 216 files. control.nacp: Undertale - 8-4, Ltd. Staged: data/ 8 files, 179,808,865 bytes.
horizon.sample_refused_because: Undertale's main.npdm declares 64-bit instructions and a 64-bit address space, so it is AArch64 and is refused at identification. The package reads completely first; the refusal is about the instruction set, not about the container or the keys. branding/ carries no 32-bit Horizon title, so no end-to-end Switch export can succeed from the samples in this repo.
horizon.aarch64_note: refused by name, for a loose NSO0/NRO0 and for an NSP alike; a Cortex-A7 cannot execute AArch64 at all
horizon.ipc: HIPC/CMIF transport complete; sm: implemented, no device services yet
horizon.svc_abi_32bit: derived from the AArch64 ABI, documented as D1/D2/D3 in extra/horizon2mvii/include/horizon_svc.h

package_launch.argv: MVII launches an application by its .virtua and passes that path as argv[0] and nothing else; argc is 1. There is no command line on the device.
package_launch.resolver: vwine_package_resolve_image in extra/virtua/wine/source/vwine_package.c, shared by both front-ends
package_launch.explicit_path: a path given on the command line still wins, for bring-up; the package is consulted only when none was given
package_launch.was_broken: both front-ends read argv[1], so every dashboard launch printed a usage line and exited. Fixed 2026-07-30 after the device console showed exactly that for Terraria and Undertale.
package_launch.export_check: `executable` is re-hashed in the built package and again in the delivered export, because it is the one file the front-end opens
